native_realtime_claim_requires: causal output or a separately declared finite delay
tracking_loop_effective_fps divided by source_fps at least 1.0
sustained backlog growth no greater than 0 frames per second
frame service-time p50, p95 and deadline-miss rate reported
bounded end-to-end output age including compute and buffering
primary and repeat runs on the same hardware and harness
failure_label: If throughput is below source FPS without a declared drop policy,
label the profile near-realtime rather than native realtime.

required_if_used: quality evaluation under the same policy

pareto_dimensions: IDSW, per-video IDSW, IDF1 and identity continuity
HOTA, FP, FN, fragments and coverage
effective FPS, loop-FPS and realtime factor
service p50/p95, deadline misses and stage timing
algorithmic delay, queue growth and end-to-end output age
peak RSS, CUDA memory, repeatability and deployment complexity
selection: Reject candidates that fail any hard operational gate.
Among eligible candidates, retain the non-dominated Pareto set.
Select the candidate matching the declared live use case and report
all remaining trade-offs; do not create a post-hoc accuracy score.

comparison_limitations: The authorities were run at different commits and times.
Balanced enabled association debug while Fast did not.
The manifests do not bind a complete CPU and GPU inventory.
A speed winner cannot be selected from these values.

invariants: same commit, Python environment, hardware, video, GT and detector
purpose: Screen operational semantics before deeper Fast accuracy tuning.
This bounded run cannot authorize the final full-13 speed claim.

next_step: Dry-run and validate both bounded harness orders.
Run primary and reverse repeat only after every invariant is visible.
Audit quality, runtime, lineage and recursive zero-MP4 together.
